reuse.why: Fintegra is wired through the existing withBankAccountLinkGuard for the duplicate-link refusal, and both linking and downloading go through shared functions (linkBankSyncAccount, downloadSingleAccountTransactions) that the other providers also use.

duplication.why: Instead of cloning another provider's link and download code, the diff collapses the five link copies and the Pluggy.ai/Akahu download copies into shared functions, so Fintegra adds only thin wrappers.

placement.why: Link logic stays in accounts/app.ts, download in sync.ts, URL in server-config, types in types/models; client provider maps are extended only where exhaustive types require it.

scope.why: To add one provider it rewrites the linking of all five existing providers and merges two download functions, an unrequested refactor that also flattens real per-provider differences (Akahu's transactions-only sync event, inserting mask for every provider).

maintainability.why: The end state is easier to extend, but the shared link helper has no parameter for the event-table variation it absorbed and the generic BankSyncExternalAccount type forces GoCardless-specific reshaping at its call site, so reviewers must audit five providers for drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The new handler is registered through withBankAccountLinkGuard like the other providers and uses the shared link and download functions.

disguised_duplication.where: Duplicated provider code is removed into shared functions, not reshaped.
